The selector uses x = ( B ~ , ρ ~ g , κ ~ ) x=(\widetilde{B},\widetilde{\rho}_{g},\widetilde{\kappa}) , with B ~ = log 2 ⁡ ( B / 56 ) , ρ ~ g = ( ρ g − 1 ) / 7 , κ ~ = ( κ − 1 ) / 2 . \widetilde{B}=\log_{2}(B/56),\qquad\widetilde{\rho}_{g}=(\rho_{g}-1)/7,\qquad\widetilde{\kappa}=(\kappa-1)/2. These constants are fixed engineering normalization scales rather than fitted model parameters. The 56-MiB reference corresponds to 32,768 tokens per node under our BF16, hidden-dimension-7,168 workload, and the log transform gives equal spacing to multiplicative changes in payload. For our eight-Rail topology, 7 = R − 1 7=R-1 scales the range from balanced traffic ( ρ g = 1 \rho_{g}=1 ) toward the single-Rail extreme. The factor 2 for κ \kappa maps the low-contention workload ( κ ≃ 1 \kappa\simeq 1 ) and the high-contention workload ( κ ≃ 3 \kappa\simeq 3 ) to approximately 0 and 1. These scales are specific to the calibrated configuration and are re-established when the topology or workload regime changes. We construct anchors only from repeatable measurements. Both Joint and a candidate alternative must satisfy p 90 / p 10 ≤ 1.2 p_{90}/p_{10}\leq 1.2 , limiting the accepted run-to-run spread to 20%. We further require p 10 ​ ( Joint ) / p 90 ​ ( candidate ) ≥ 1.05 p_{10}(\mathrm{Joint})/p_{90}(\mathrm{candidate})\geq 1.05 , so that the alternative retains at least a 5% advantage under a conservative cross-quantile comparison. For low-contention development cases, known equivalent-path controls are additionally required to agree within 10%; otherwise the point is rejected as noisy. We evaluate 24 requests on H800: 12 development-regression requests and 12 requests not used to construct the frozen table. Each path uses five warmup iterations, followed by interleaved measurements; we report the median of the first 10 samples. We therefore use only the seven actual path switches to quantify selector benefit. A.4 Packing Overhead Permutation-only and Joint require per-wave packing.
